purpose: Mathematical and kinematic prerequisite only; not simulated response or independent physics validation

profiles.benign: copy shared prefix through B; for 0 <= s = t-B <= 1, rho(B) + (s-s*s/2)/240; then rho(B)+1/480

assumptions: Identical initial state, past inputs and prefix noise distribution under a causal plant and estimator imply identical observation and alarm distributions through the branch, including any computation and delivery delay; an earlier effective deadline only strengthens the bound.
q is the probability of an alarm by B on the common history; timely success on the ambiguous crossing is at most q and benign shared-prefix alarm probability is at least q.
The ambiguous pairs are fraction alpha of crossings; the remaining crossings are optimistically assumed perfectly detected.

The nuisance episode rate bound requires lambda_b benign opportunities per hour with common clear and rearm between them and no future-event credit or relabeling. Without these assumptions only a run-level alarm probability bound follows.
The exploratory alpha and lambda_b values are hypothetical, not measured and not a frozen prospective operating distribution.
derivation: q_min = max(0, 1 - (1-target)/alpha); nuisance episodes/hour >= lambda_b*q_min; necessary compatibility with the episode limit requires lambda_b*q_min <= limit.
limitations: Normalized ratio and rate bounds are kinematic facts only and do not validate a physical envelope.
No response simulation, actual critical speed, geometry, hidden inputs, native generation, features, estimator outputs or ground-truth datasets are used.
Always-on or merged alarms require duration and availability accounting and are not covered by the episode formula.
No empirical risk confidence interval or posterior is computed; no unconditional P4 impossibility is established.
